summary: Third-pass adversarial audit. Rather than trust verdict_01's gold_standard_met=true, I independently re-derived the highest-risk evidence-validity items from source: (R1.1) SDLG is a GENUINE gradient-attribution implementation, not a stub — nli.py:174 computes A_i=||z_i ⊙ ∇z_i L||_2 by backpropping a contradiction-class cross-entropy through the DeBERTa embeddings, and nli_server.py:135 computes the first-order substitution score s_ij=(z_i−v_j)·∇z_i L / (‖·‖‖·‖), exactly Aichberger 2025 Alg.2; (R1.2/1.3) greedy reproduces Farquhar/Kuhn Alg.1, connected is order-independent union-find, kernel is the von Neumann entropy of the heat kernel exp(−tL) (clustering.py:264-318) and is correctly cited as Nikitin 2024; (R1.5) the τ-gate is now ENFORCED identically in BOTH arms — strategy_proposal reads cfg(entropy_threshold) and collapses to the dominant cluster when entropy≤τ (phased_orchestrator.py:683,717-729), SDLG returns early on the same key (1014,1035) — closing the VALIDATION_BRIEF 'hardcoded tau=0.0' fairness nit, with a stage test asserting both branch and collapse; (R4.1) pass_at_k is the unbiased Chen product form; (R4.2) diversity is difflib-structural over final patches, NOT the branching NLI; (R5) the stratification/off-mode/set-valued analysis is runnable with a single shared split threshold; (R6.3) per-arm tokens come from extra.response.usage; (R8.5) all six stage groups (a–f) are covered across the test modules; (R9.1) the base model is config-driven through every sub-call and tested. I found ONE real but secondary gap iter 0/1 missed: run_branching.py's documented `--diversity-method none --temperature T` path set only sample_temperature (the proposer reference), never the base agent's model_kwargs temperature, so a 'none' run via that entry point would decode at the config default temp 0.0 — a deterministic strawman that violates R2.4 ('Vanilla MUST sample at T>0'). The canonical baseline path (run_resample_baseline.py) was always correct, so this did not corrupt the headline design, but the flag's own help text promised it applied to the 'none' arm. I fixed it with a pure, unit-tested helper vanilla_samples_at_temperature() that injects sample_temperature into the base agent's decoding ONLY for the 'none' arm (treatment arms stay greedy and get diversity from the proposer/SDLG), mirroring run_resample_baseline. I also routed the two raw entropy_threshold reads through the central cfg() helper (R8.2) and de-pinned a stale '33 passing' test count in RESULTS.md. 42 tests pass (was 41), py_compile clean, all four driver --help smokes pass. Every BLOCKER passes on the spec's readiness bar (wiring + correctness proven; executed numbers explicitly permitted to await the GPU runs per the DONE section). gold_standard_met stays true and blocking_gaps empty — consistent with iter 1 and now independently re-derived plus one correctness hardening, which is the stability the DONE bar asks for. The multi-hour vLLM+SWE-bench matched-k runs remain the human-only step that turns the wired metrics into reported numbers; they are in next_actions, not blocking_gaps. No GOLD_STANDARD.md edit was warranted (no derivable rigor-increasing correction found), so no spec amendment was written.

R1_faithfulness.notes: Independently re-derived SDLG gradient/substitution math against the paper this iteration — genuine, not a stub. tau gate now enforced identically in both arms (was a hardcoded tau=0.0 nit); kernel correctly cited as Nikitin 2024 KLE.

issues_found.title: run_branching.py --diversity-method none --temperature decoded the base agent at config temp 0.0 (deterministic strawman) instead of sample_temperature
issues_found.rationale: The 'none' arm's only diversity source is base-agent sampling, so a temp-0 run violates R2.4 ('Vanilla MUST sample at T>0'). The flag help text claimed it applied to the 'none' arm but only sample_temperature (the proposer reference) was updated, not the base agent's model_kwargs. The canonical run_resample_baseline.py path was always correct (it injects temperature at :108), so the headline design was never corrupted — but this exposed entry point silently was not. Fixed with a unit-tested pure helper that injects sample_temperature ONLY for the 'none' arm (treatment arms stay greedy by design).

issues_found.title: Two entropy_threshold reads bypassed the central cfg() default helper (R8.2)
issues_found.rationale: phased_orchestrator.py read entropy_threshold via raw .get(..., 0.0) in two sites while branching_defaults.py's docstring instructs reading every fallback through cfg(). The literal matched the central default so behavior was identical, but the duplication is the exact divergence-risk R8.2 exists to prevent. Routed both through cfg().

issues_found.title: RESULTS.md pinned a stale '33 passing' test count (actual: 42)
issues_found.rationale: The count drifts every iteration that adds a test, becoming a small factual inaccuracy in the writeup artifact. Replaced the hardcoded number with the reproduction command (python -m pytest tests/ -q).

issues_found.title: Existing results/branching artifacts have degenerate post-search entropy (log 5 uniform), so R5.2 stratification is not yet exercisable on real data
issues_found.rationale: Those artifacts predate the tau-gate-enforcement fix and branched all 5 strategies at tau=0, so every instance shows entropy=1.609. The stratification machinery is correct and runs; it needs the new matched-k GPU runs (gate enforced) to produce varied entropy. Human/GPU step, recorded in next_actions.
